report.summary: Deployment of revision orders-00002 introduced a code change storing totals as Decimal, which crashes serialize_order_v2 with 'TypeError: Object of type Decimal is not JSON serializable' during json.dumps validation. This unhandled exception caused POST /orders to fail with HTTP 500, leading the frontend to return HTTP 502 for POST /checkout. Logs and metrics show the 5xx error rate spiking from 0% to nearly 100% immediately following the release of orders-00002.

Deployment of revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable, causing POST /charge to crash with an unhandled KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL'. The resulting HTTP 500 errors from payments cascaded as HTTP 502 responses through orders to frontend checkout requests. Rolling back payments to payments-00001 restores service.

Revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing the database connection pool to become exhausted under traffic. Requests to orders failed with SQLAlchemy QueuePool TimeoutErrors (HTTP 503), which caused frontend POST /checkout requests to fail with HTTP 502/503. Rolling back orders to orders-00001 restores the connection pool capacity.

Revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE from lru:256 to unbounded, causing frontend memory consumption to exceed the 512 MiB container limit. The container was OOM-killed (exit code 137), leading to 503 errors on incoming GET /products requests during restarts. Evidence includes critical memory limit alerts and OOM termination logs on frontend-00002.

Requests to POST /checkout are failing with 502/504 errors because orders times out after 400ms waiting for payments POST /charge. Within payments, calls to the external fraud-check provider api.fraudshield.example.com are exceeding their 300ms SLO and failing to respond in time. Because this is caused by an external dependency degradation rather than a code deployment, no rollback is proposed.

Revision orders-00002 introduced Decimal values for order totals, which caused unhandled TypeError exceptions in serialize_order_v2 because Decimal is not JSON serializable. This led POST /orders to return HTTP 500, which in turn caused frontend POST /checkout requests to fail with HTTP 502 Bad Gateway. Log entries show the unhandled serialization error on orders-00002 immediately following its deployment.

Revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable during a migration to Secret Manager, causing payments.py to crash with KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL' on all POST /charge requests. This 500 failure cascades upstream as 502 errors to orders and frontend /checkout endpoints. Metrics confirm a 100% 5xx error rate on payments starting immediately when payments-00002 was deployed.

The orders service experienced database connection pool exhaustion after revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1. Concurrent requests timed out waiting for a database connection with QueuePool limit errors, returning HTTP 503 to frontend and causing frontend POST /checkout to fail with HTTP 502. Rolling back orders to revision orders-00001 restores the connection pool size and resolves the issue.

Revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE to unbounded, causing rapid memory growth that exceeded the 512 MiB container memory limit. The instance was repeatedly terminated with exit code 137 (OOMKilled), returning 503 errors on GET /products during restarts.

The external fraud-check provider api.fraudshield.example.com became unresponsive, exceeding its 300ms SLO during payment processing in the payments service. This caused downstream calls from the orders service to time out after 0.4s and return HTTP 504, resulting in HTTP 502 failures on frontend POST /checkout. No recent deployments occurred across any service, so no rollback is proposed.

Deployment of revision orders-00002 introduced Decimal objects into order totals without appropriate JSON serialization support, causing POST /orders requests to crash with TypeError in serialize_order_v2. Frontend checkouts failed with HTTP 502 as orders returned HTTP 500 errors. Rolling back orders to orders-00001 will resolve the issue.

Revision payments-00002 removed the PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL environment variable as part of moving gateway settings to Secret Manager, but the application code still accessed env['PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL']. This caused every POST /charge request to fail with an unhandled KeyError: 'PAYMENT_GATEWAY_URL' returning HTTP 500, cascading upstream as HTTP 502 errors in orders and frontend /checkout. Rolling back payments to revision payments-00001 restores the missing environment variable and fixes the errors.

Revision orders-00002 reduced DB_POOL_SIZE from 10 to 1, causing SQLAlchemy QueuePool connection exhaustion under concurrent requests. As a result, orders failed with QueuePool TimeoutErrors and returned HTTP 503, which caused frontend checkout requests to fail with HTTP 502.

Deployment of frontend revision frontend-00002 changed PRODUCT_CACHE from 'lru:256' to 'unbounded' to cache catalogue responses, causing container memory to rapidly exceed the 512 MiB limit. The containers were repeatedly terminated with exit code 137 (OOMKilled), leading to 503 errors on GET /products during instance crashes and restarts.

Checkout requests failed with 502/504 errors because orders timed out waiting for payments POST /charge. Revision payments-00002 ('chore(deps): bump httpx to 0.28.1') caused outgoing calls to the fraud-check provider (api.fraudshield.example.com) to hang indefinitely, breaching upstream timeouts. Rolling back payments to payments-00001 will resolve the issue.

This causes POST /orders to return HTTP 500, leading to HTTP 502 responses on frontend POST /checkout. Rolling back orders to orders-00001 will resolve the issue.

Rolling back orders to orders-00001 restores pool capacity and resolves the failures.

The external fraud-check provider api.fraudshield.example.com became unresponsive, exceeding its SLO and stalling payments POST /charge requests. Log evidence confirms the provider latency warnings in payments coinciding with downstream timeout errors in orders and frontend without any recent deployments.
